output.brief: The rise in Corvane's mishandled bags is very probably not a handler problem. Since 1 Sep, check-in has used a new tag stock (Fennick). Tags printed on it fail automatic reading about 12% of the time, against about 1.5% on the old stock. Those bags go to the manual encode desk, where waits grew from 7 to over 30 minutes. About 91% of the encode-path bags that missed their flight reached the lateral after it closed. Bags read automatically show no rise. Pelion, handled by the same Tessaly crew pool, did not rise. On 14–16 Oct, counters using old stock from stores failed at 1.6% while kiosks on the new stock failed at 12.1%. I'm fairly sure of this. What remains unknown is whether the stock itself is faulty or the printer heat settings don't suit it. Next steps: do not send the breach notice or hold the fee. Switch counters and kiosks back to Brackwater stock, since five weeks of it are in stores. Test Fennick stock with the printer maker's settings. Hold off on a defect claim against Fennick until that test is done. Asking the airport for an extra encode workstation in the evening is a reasonable stopgap. Tessaly's crew inexperience is worth monitoring, but it doesn't explain the rise.
